## Learning goals

You will see a treatment effect that is not the same size in every subgroup. The file is the social-pressure experiment again, the heterogeneous-effects section of QSS 4.4.2. The moderator is `primary2004`: did the household vote in the 2004 primary? The outcome is `primary2006`. The contrast is Neighbors against Control.

A larger effect in one subgroup is a clue about where the mailing matters. It is not yet the mechanism. The subgroup was not a second experiment you designed to isolate social pressure from every other difference between 2004 voters and everyone else.

## 1. Two effects

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
social <- read_csv("data/social.csv") %>%
  filter(messages %in% c("Control", "Neighbors"))
social %>%
  group_by(primary2004, messages) %>%
  summarise(turnout = mean(primary2006), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

Among households that voted in 2004, turnout is about 48.2 percent under Neighbors and 38.6 percent under Control. The gap is about 9.6 points. Among households that did not vote in 2004, the rates are about 30.6 and 23.7 percent. The gap is about 6.9 points.

The Neighbors mailing is associated with a larger increase where people had voted before. That is an interaction: the effect of the mailing changes with the moderator. It does not name the psychological step that produced the extra votes, and a search across many subgroups will eventually find a gap by chance.
